name: SeaHash
workload: generic byte-buffer hashing throughput (no specific dataset or size stated in the source)
claimed_speedup: ~3-20% faster than xxHash and MetroHash; ~5.9-6.7 GB/s vs CityHash ~1 GB/s, MurmurHash ~2.6 GB/s, FNV ~0.5 GB/s (author's own numbers)
tradeoffs: Canonical implementation is Rust; unofficial C/C++/Go ports exist (e.g. jroivas/seahash, briandowns/libseahash) but were not verified here. Not cryptographically secure. Scalar, portable design with no SIMD/hardware-intrinsic requirement, which is part of the pitch vs xxHash/MetroHash on platforms lacking those optimizations.
caveats: Numbers are first-party (crate docs / README), no compiler or compiler flags stated, CPU given only as a generic "2.5 GHz CPU" with no model, and no linked reproducible benchmark harness was found to open. Repo has had no commits since Oct 2023 (~3 years).
found_via: HN Algolia search 'fast hash function' -> docs.rs/seahash/2.0.0 story; corroborated via HN Algolia 'hash function benchmark' search and the project's own blog post https://ticki.github.io/blog/designing-a-good-non-cryptographic-hash-function/
